intro: Section 23.3 covers group psychotherapy: how groups are classified and run, patient selection, preparation, group size, frequency and composition, the therapeutic factors that drive change, the therapist's role, inpatient and self-help groups, combined individual and group therapy, psychodrama and the ethical and legal issues groups raise. A dashed box adds what is known about groups run online.
objectives: Compare the major group orientations (supportive, psychodynamic, self-help, cognitive-behavioral) (Table 23-4).
Select and prepare patients for group therapy, and choose size, frequency, composition and an open or closed format.
Define the therapeutic factors of group therapy and recognize them in action (Table 23-5).
Describe inpatient groups, self-help groups and combined individual and group therapy.
Name the roles and techniques of psychodrama.
Handle confidentiality, aggression and sexual behavior in groups.
